26cv257|2026-09-29.case: PHI Health, LLC v. California Physicians' Service
26cv257|2026-09-29.summary: PHI Health sought to enforce a $55,066.49 IDR award against Blue Shield under an implied right of action in the No Surprises Act and under Section 9 of the Federal Arbitration Act. The court held the NSA creates no implied private right to enforce IDR awards, and Section 9 does not apply. It dismissed the federal claims without leave to amend and declined jurisdiction over state claims.

26cv4326|2026-09-23.case: California Spine and Neurosurgery Institute d/b/a San Jose Neurospine v. Microsoft Corp. et al.
26cv4326|2026-09-23.summary: A provider sought to enforce a $71,888.85 No Surprises Act IDR award against an insurer and a plan sponsor through ERISA, FAA confirmation, implied-right-of-action and state-law claims. The court held the Act gives providers no private right of action to enforce IDR awards, FAA Section 9 cannot confirm them, the ERISA claims lack standing, and state claims cannot circumvent that gap. It dismissed everything without leave to amend.

25-2204|2026-09-17.case: East Coast Advanced Plastic Surgery, LLC v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Co.
25-2204|2026-09-17.summary: A provider with over $3 million in IDR awards sued Cigna for a declaration that Cigna owes the awards and violated the No Surprises Act by not paying. The Second Circuit held the Act contains no implied private right of action to enforce IDR awards, because it assigns enforcement to federal agencies and states. The Declaratory Judgment Act supplied no independent claim, so the dismissal was affirmed.

26cv4774|2026-09-02.case: Jeffrey Farkas, M.D., LLC v. Aetna Life Insurance Company
26cv4774|2026-09-02.summary: A medical practice that won a $88,163.72 IDR award sued Aetna on state and common-law claims for nonpayment. The court granted Aetna's motion to dismiss under the election-of-remedies doctrine: by choosing the optional IDR process, with its administrative enforcement, the provider could not also sue on the same facts. It did not decide whether the No Surprises Act gives a private right of action.

26cv2954|2026-08-05.case: PHI Health, LLC v. Health Care Service Corp.
26cv2954|2026-08-05.summary: PHI Health sought to enforce or confirm No Surprises Act arbitration awards against HCSC. The court dismissed the complaint, holding the Act creates no implied private right of action and does not permit judicial confirmation. The FAA and Illinois arbitration claims failed for lack of a written arbitration agreement; the ERISA and consumer fraud claims also failed. PHI may seek to file an amended complaint.

25cv1168|2026-07-21.case: Shareef Jandali Plastic Surgery, LLC v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Co.
25cv1168|2026-07-21.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm and enforce a $31,500 IDR award that Cigna had not paid. The court held that the No Surprises Act lets providers sue to enforce binding IDR awards, because of its "binding" and "shall be made" payment language, and that the no-judicial-review clause does not bar confirmation. It denied Cigna's motion to dismiss and confirmed the award.

25cv1367|2026-07-21.case: Shareef Jandali Plastic Surgery, LLC v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Co.
25cv1367|2026-07-21.summary: A provider sought confirmation of four IDR awards against Cigna, withdrawing one. The court granted summary judgment in part, confirming three awards totaling $74,190.20, holding the No Surprises Act lets providers sue to enforce binding IDR awards; it denied dismissal and rejected Cigna's coverage-denial defense. It allowed a motion for IDR fees and pre-judgment interest within 21 days.

25cv1476|2026-07-21.case: Northeast Plastic Surgery Center, LLC v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Company
25cv1476|2026-07-21.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm a $20,800 No Surprises Act IDR award against Cigna, which moved to dismiss. The court held the Act gives providers a right to sue to enforce binding IDR awards, and its no-judicial-review clause does not bar confirmation. It denied dismissal, granted summary judgment confirming the award, and withdrew claims were not decided.

25cv1472|2026-07-21.case: New England PA, LLC v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Company
25cv1472|2026-07-21.summary: New England withdrew five of six IDR disputes and sought confirmation of the last, a $10,000 award. The court held the No Surprises Act lets providers enforce binding awards and its no-judicial-review clause doesn't bar confirmation, so it denied dismissal and confirmed the award. Post-judgment interest runs from judgment; pre-judgment interest and attorneys' fees were declined as inadequately briefed, with leave to move for IDR fees and pre-judgment interest.

24cv9342|2026-07-15.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. v. Kaiser Foundation Health Plan
24cv9342|2026-07-15.summary: SpecialtyCare asked the court to enforce a $114,813 IDR award against Kaiser. The court held the No Surprises Act gives providers no implied private right of action, because Congress gave three federal agencies enforcement power, and dismissed the FAA § 9 and ERISA claims. It held the Act does not preempt state-law claims but dismissed all of them, allowing an amended complaint on the UCL claim only.

250606|2026-07-08.case: PHI Health, L.L.C. v. Custom Design Benefits, L.L.C.
250606|2026-07-08.summary: PHI Health, an air ambulance company, sued to confirm and enforce two No Surprises Act IDR awards under the Act, the Federal Arbitration Act and Ohio's Arbitration Act. The appeals court affirmed dismissal. It held the No Surprises Act gives providers no private right of action to enforce IDR awards, and that the awards are not enforceable under the federal or Ohio arbitration statutes.

25cv12406|2026-06-23.case: PHI Health, LLC v. Health Care Service Corp. d/b/a Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas
25cv12406|2026-06-23.summary: A provider sought to enforce an IDR award under the No Surprises Act, FAA Section 9 and declaratory judgment law, plus an Illinois fraud claim. The court held the Act gives no private right of action and Section 9 does not apply, dismissing those counts with prejudice; declaratory relief failed for lack of a private right of action. The Illinois claim was dismissed without prejudice; amendment is allowed by 7/14/2026.

25cv130|2026-06-09.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. et al. v. CareFirst of Maryland, Inc.
25cv130|2026-06-09.summary: Providers sued CareFirst to recover unpaid IDR awards under the No Surprises Act and other laws. The court held the Act gives providers an implied private right of action to enforce unpaid final IDR awards, denying dismissal of that count. It dismissed the express-cause-of-action count and reserved on the remaining counts.

24cv12935|2026-06-02.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. et al. v. Health Care Service Corp. d/b/a BCBS Illinois
24cv12935|2026-06-02.summary: Providers sought to enforce an unpaid No Surprises Act IDR award under ERISA, FAA Section 9, and an implied right of action. The court dismissed these claims with prejudice: underpayment falls outside ERISA, Section 9 requires an arbitration agreement, and the Act's judicial-review limit and HHS penalty scheme preclude an implied private right of action. State claims were dismissed without prejudice.

24cv12945|2026-06-02.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. et al. v. Health Care Service Corp. d/b/a BCBS Texas
24cv12945|2026-06-02.summary: Healthcare providers sued an insurer to enforce an unpaid No Surprises Act IDR award, under ERISA, FAA Section 9, and the Act itself. The court dismissed the federal claims, holding the Act gives providers no implied right to sue to enforce awards, FAA Section 9 requires an arbitration agreement, and ERISA does not cover underpayment. It declined jurisdiction over state-law claims.

24cv12902|2026-06-02.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. et al. v. Health Care Service Corp. d/b/a BCBS New Mexico
24cv12902|2026-06-02.summary: Providers sought to enforce an unpaid No Surprises Act IDR award through ERISA, FAA Section 9, and the Act itself. The court dismissed the federal claims with prejudice: underpayment falls outside ERISA's zone of interests, Section 9 requires an arbitration agreement, and the Act gives providers no implied right of action. It dismissed state-law claims without prejudice, declining supplemental jurisdiction.

25cv498|2026-04-15.case: Agag v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Co.
25cv498|2026-04-15.summary: A physician asked the court to confirm five No Surprises Act IDR awards against Cigna and to order payment. The court held it has federal question jurisdiction and that a provider may seek confirmation under the NSA, not the FAA, because confirmation is a summary, non-merits step. It confirmed the awards ($142,567.99) but dismissed the FAA and NSA damages claims.

25cv5068|2026-04-07.case: Advanced Vascular Associates v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv5068|2026-04-07.summary: An out-of-network provider asked the court to confirm unpaid IDR awards under the Federal Arbitration Act or to enforce them directly under the No Surprises Act. The court granted the insurer judgment on the pleadings. IDR is statutory, not an agreed arbitration, so FAA Section 9 does not apply, and the Act gives providers no private right of action to enforce awards.

25cv57|2026-04-01.case: Jeffrey Farkas, M.D., LLC v. 1199SEIU National Benefit Fund
25cv57|2026-04-01.summary: A medical practice asked the court to confirm a $32,000 No Surprises Act IDR award. The court dismissed for lack of jurisdiction and denied confirmation, holding the Act does not incorporate FAA Section 9 or imply a private right of action for providers, the FAA confers no jurisdiction, and the practice lacked standing on a denied claim. It found the fund's motion to vacate timely but did not decide vacatur.

25cv1277|2026-03-30.case: NeuroShield Network SE, LLC v. Phoenix Administrators, LLC d/b/a Performance Health
25cv1277|2026-03-30.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm and enforce an approximately $15,400 No Surprises Act IDR award under Section 9 of the Federal Arbitration Act. The court held the Act creates no implied right of action to enforce IDR awards, since Congress incorporated only parts of Section 10 and provided administrative enforcement. It dismissed the petition for lack of subject matter jurisdiction and found amendment futile.

25cv2938|2026-03-30.case: T.V. Seshan, M.D., P.C. v. Aetna, Inc.
25cv2938|2026-03-30.summary: A neurology practice asked the court to confirm an IDR award against Aetna under the No Surprises Act and Section 9 of the Federal Arbitration Act. The court dismissed, holding the Act creates no implied private right of action and, by allowing judicial review only to vacate awards, forecloses FAA confirmation. It did not reach the proper-party argument.

25cv2320|2026-03-27.case: PHI Health, LLC v. Optimum Choice, Inc.
25cv2320|2026-03-27.summary: An air ambulance provider asked the court to confirm and enforce an unpaid IDR award against an insurer, which moved to dismiss. The court denied the motion, holding the No Surprises Act impliedly gives providers a narrow private right of action to enforce binding IDR awards unpaid after 30 days. It did not decide the Federal Arbitration Act theory.

25cv198|2026-03-17.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. et al. v. Meritain Health, Inc.
25cv198|2026-03-17.summary: Healthcare providers sued Meritain Health seeking to enforce rights under the No Surprises Act. The court granted the motion to dismiss, holding the Act creates no private right of action, following the Fifth Circuit's Guardian Flight decision. Plaintiffs also could not get around that omission by using a state law theory to enforce a federal right.

20250011|2026-02-16.summary: Providers asked the Court of Chancery to confirm unpaid No Surprises Act IDR awards or, alternatively, for account stated, quantum meruit and unjust enrichment relief. The court held IDR is not arbitration, so it lacked jurisdiction, and alternatively that the Act creates no implied private right of action; it dismissed those counts and account stated with prejudice. Quantum meruit and unjust enrichment were dismissed without prejudice.

25cv1225|2026-02-13.case: Worldwide Aircraft Services, Inc. v. United Healthcare
25cv1225|2026-02-13.summary: A provider that won a No Surprises Act IDR award against United Healthcare asked the court to confirm it. The court granted the insurer's motion to dismiss with prejudice for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, holding the Act's IDR provisions create no federal cause of action and IDR awards are not enforceable under the FAA. It also ordered the provider to show cause why Rule 11 sanctions should not issue.

25cv2231|2026-02-04.case: Worldwide Aircraft Services, Inc. d/b/a Jet ICU v. Aetna Life Insurance Co.
25cv2231|2026-02-04.summary: Jet ICU asked the court to confirm a No Surprises Act IDR award against Aetna and enter judgment on it. The court granted Aetna's motion to dismiss, holding the Act gives providers no private right of action to confirm or enforce IDR awards. It also found the FAA and Florida Arbitration Code inapplicable without an agreement. The petition was dismissed with prejudice.

25cv223|2026-01-27.case: GuardION Medical LLC v. MedCost Benefit Services LLC
25cv223|2026-01-27.summary: GuardION Medical asked the court to confirm No Surprises Act IDR awards under the Federal Arbitration Act. The court denied the petition and granted the motion to dismiss, holding the Act gives no private right of action to enforce IDR awards and the FAA doesn't independently confer jurisdiction, since no arbitration agreement was alleged. Dismissal was without prejudice.

25cv224|2025-12-23.case: SpecialtyCare, Inc. et al. v. Aetna, Inc.
25cv224|2025-12-23.summary: SpecialtyCare, a neuromonitoring provider, sought confirmation of No Surprises Act IDR awards against Aetna, plus state-law claims. The court held the Act creates no private right of action to enforce IDR awards, because Congress allowed vacatur but not confirmation. It granted Aetna judgment on that part and remanded the state claims to state court.

25cv12593|2025-12-18.case: North Jersey Neurosurgical Associates, P.A. v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv12593|2025-12-18.summary: A neurosurgical practice sued under the No Surprises Act to recover $299,232.67 in IDR awards and cross-moved to confirm an arbitration award. Relying on Modern Orthopaedics of New Jersey v. Premera Blue Cross, the court held it lacked jurisdiction. It denied both the insurer's motion to dismiss and the provider's cross-motion, and dismissed the complaint with prejudice.

25cv12682|2025-12-18.case: Comprehensive OBGYN, P.A. v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv12682|2025-12-18.summary: A provider sued under the No Surprises Act to recover $17,127.88 in IDR awards and cross-moved to confirm the award. The court, relying on another District of New Jersey decision, concluded it lacks jurisdiction. It denied both motions and dismissed the complaint with prejudice.

25cv1701|2025-12-18.case: Neuromon Professionals LLC v. Aetna Life Insurance Co.
25cv1701|2025-12-18.summary: Neuromon Professionals moved to confirm two No Surprises Act IDR awards, of $11,200 and $11,700, against Aetna. The court denied the motion and dismissed the complaint with prejudice, concluding it lacks jurisdiction over the matter. It relied on the reasoning of Modern Orthopaedics of New Jersey v. Premera Blue Cross.

25cv1158|2025-12-11.case: Worldwide Aircraft Services, Inc. d/b/a Jet ICU v. Freedom Life Insurance Co.
25cv1158|2025-12-11.summary: Jet ICU, an air ambulance provider, asked the court to confirm a $35,354.75 IDR award against Freedom Life. The court dismissed the complaint without prejudice for lack of subject matter jurisdiction, holding the No Surprises Act gives providers no private right of action to confirm or enforce IDR awards because it incorporates only FAA § 10(a), not § 9.

25cv12526|2025-12-08.case: Mitchell F. Reiter, M.D., P.C. v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv12526|2025-12-08.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm two No Surprises Act arbitration awards under the Federal Arbitration Act and to enforce payment. The court dismissed the claims, holding the Act gives providers no private right to sue to enforce or confirm awards: it incorporates only FAA § 10(a), limits judicial review, and relies on administrative enforcement.

25cv499|2025-12-05.case: T.V. Seshan, M.D., P.C. v. Blue Cross Blue Shield Association et al.
25cv499|2025-12-05.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm No Surprises Act arbitration awards under Section 9 of the Federal Arbitration Act and to enforce them under the Act. The court dismissed the complaints and denied confirmation. Section 9 does not apply to IDR awards, and the Act gives providers no private right of action. The court denied leave to amend as futile.

25cv12032|2025-12-03.case: Interventional Pain Management v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv12032|2025-12-03.summary: An out-of-network pain management provider asked the court to confirm No Surprises Act IDR determinations under the Federal Arbitration Act and order payment of $29,719.70. The court denied confirmation and dismissed both counts. It held the IDR process is not an FAA arbitration, and the Act creates no express or implied private right to enforce awards.

25cv2022|2025-12-02.case: Tamagnini v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv2022|2025-12-02.summary: A podiatrist asked the court to confirm two No Surprises Act IDR determinations under the Federal Arbitration Act and order Horizon to pay $24,836.95. The court dismissed both counts. It held the IDR process is not an arbitration under the FAA, and the Act creates no express or implied private right to enforce awards. The motion was unopposed.

25cv14769|2025-12-02.case: Douglas Spiel, M.D., P.A. v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv14769|2025-12-02.summary: A radiology practice asked the court to confirm an IDR award under the Federal Arbitration Act and order Horizon to pay the unpaid balance. The court denied confirmation and dismissed both counts. It held the IDR process is not an arbitration under the FAA, and the No Surprises Act creates no express or implied private right to enforce awards.

25cv5679|2025-12-01.case: Garden State Pain Management v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv5679|2025-12-01.summary: A medical provider asked the court to confirm an IDR award under the Federal Arbitration Act and order the insurer to pay $69,759.25. The court granted the insurer's motion to dismiss and denied confirmation, holding the IDR process is not a consensual arbitration under the FAA and the No Surprises Act gives providers no express or implied private right to enforce awards.

25cv4177|2025-12-01.case: Complete Medical Wellness LLC v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv4177|2025-12-01.summary: A neurosurgery provider asked the court to confirm an IDR award under the Federal Arbitration Act and order the insurer to pay $4,789.59. The court dismissed both counts and denied confirmation. It held the IDR process is not an FAA arbitration, and the No Surprises Act creates no express or implied private right to enforce awards.

24cv2527|2025-11-28.case: Worldwide Aircraft Services, Inc. v. United Healthcare
24cv2527|2025-11-28.summary: An air ambulance provider asked the court to confirm a No Surprises Act IDR award and enter judgment for it. The court denied the petition, holding the Act gives providers no private right of action to enforce IDR awards, and that FAA § 9 doesn't apply without an arbitration agreement. It did not reach the award's interpretation.

25cv1087|2025-11-03.case: Modern Orthopaedics of NJ v. Premera Blue Cross
25cv1087|2025-11-03.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm its IDR award. The court dismissed: FAA Section 9 does not apply because IDR is not arbitration and Section 9 gives no federal jurisdiction, and the No Surprises Act implies no federal right of action to enforce awards, given administrative enforcement and the bar on judicial review. The court said the provider has a right to be paid and state-law claims remain available.

25cv255|2025-08-14.case: East Coast Advanced Plastic Surgery, LLC v. Cigna Health and Life Insurance Co.
25cv255|2025-08-14.summary: The provider sought a declaration enforcing a $3 million IDR award against Cigna and a declaration that Cigna violated the No Surprises Act. The court dismissed both, holding the Act gives providers no private right of action to enforce IDR awards, because the statute bars judicial review of awards outside narrow Federal Arbitration Act exceptions. Dismissal was without prejudice.

24-10561|2025-06-12.case: Guardian Flight, L.L.C. v. Health Care Service Corp.
24-10561|2025-06-12.summary: Two air ambulance providers sued an insurer for failing to timely pay 33 IDR awards, also pleading ERISA and quantum meruit claims. The Fifth Circuit held the No Surprises Act contains no private right of action to enforce IDR awards, because its bar on judicial review and its administrative enforcement scheme exclude one. It also rejected the ERISA and quantum meruit claims and the amendment request.

24cv840|2024-09-18.case: Worldwide Aircraft Services, Inc. d/b/a Jet ICU v. Worldwide Insurance Services, LLC d/b/a GeoBlue
24cv840|2024-09-18.summary: An air ambulance provider asked the court to confirm a $220,204 No Surprises Act IDR award against GeoBlue. The court confirmed it and denied GeoBlue's motion to vacate, finding GeoBlue failed to show it was outside the Act or lacked notice. The court deemed waived the question whether the Act lets federal courts confirm awards, since GeoBlue did not raise it.

23cv1861|2024-05-30.case: Guardian Flight, L.L.C. v. Health Care Service Corp.
23cv1861|2024-05-30.summary: Two air ambulance providers sued an insurer to enforce No Surprises Act IDR awards, also pleading ERISA and unjust enrichment claims. The court granted the motion to dismiss, holding the Act gives providers no express or implied private cause of action to enforce awards. The ERISA claim failed for lack of standing, and the unjust enrichment claim failed. The court denied leave to amend.

24cv2832|2025-12-11.case: PHI Health, LLC v. Keating Auto Group Employee Benefit Plan Trust / Entrust, LLC
24cv2832|2025-12-11.summary: PHI Health brought a claim under an implied right of action in the No Surprises Act. The court adopted the magistrate judge's unopposed recommendation, dismissed that claim without prejudice, and dismissed the case without prejudice for lack of subject matter jurisdiction. It denied Keating's motion to dismiss and PHI Health's summary judgment motion as moot.

25cv54|2025-07-02.case: Jeffrey Farkas, M.D., LLC v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey

24cv680|2025-05-14.case: Guardian Flight LLC et al. v. Aetna Health Inc. et al.
24cv680|2025-05-14.summary: Six air ambulance companies asked the court to enforce No Surprises Act IDR awards that Aetna and Cigna allegedly paid late or not at all. The court held the Act creates a private right of action to enforce IDR awards and denied dismissal of the Act, ERISA benefits and CUTPA claims. It dismissed only the ERISA equitable-relief claim.

23cv876|2024-04-04.case: FHMC LLC v. Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Arizona, Inc.
23cv876|2024-04-04.summary: Two providers sued a Blue Cross insurer under the Affordable Care Act and No Surprises Act, plus state-law claims. The court held neither federal statute gives providers an implied private right of action, so it dismissed the federal claims and declined supplemental jurisdiction over the state claims. The court allowed an amended complaint within thirty days.

25cv6288|2025-11-25.case: Northeast Neurosurgical Associates v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv6288|2025-11-25.summary: A medical provider asked the court to confirm an IDR award under the Federal Arbitration Act and order the insurer to pay the unpaid balance. The court dismissed both counts and denied confirmation. It held the IDR process is not an FAA arbitration, and the No Surprises Act creates no express or implied private right to enforce IDR awards in court.

25cv2507|2025-11-24.case: Freeman Pain Institute, P.A. v. Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield of New Jersey
25cv2507|2025-11-24.summary: A provider asked the court to confirm a No Surprises Act IDR award under the Federal Arbitration Act and order payment of $69,587.28. The court dismissed the complaint and denied confirmation. It held the IDR process is not an FAA arbitration because there is no agreement to arbitrate, and the Act creates no express or implied private right to enforce awards.
